title: E2E suite adaptation: Supabase Auth login strategy, seed/job hooks, full existing Playwright coverage green
objective: Adapt the existing Playwright suite (~29 spec files) to the migrated stack with only test-infrastructure changes — base URLs, Supabase Auth login (seeded users + admin-minted sessions per Q-21), seed invocation, job-trigger hooks (cron:run/queue:worker) — and get the full suite green: demo journey, tenant isolation, RBAC visibility, role-403 sweep, cross-tenant Internal mode, dashboards x5, alerts queue actions, exports, a11y, visual shell (A-17).
scope: Test infrastructure: base URL to the local Vercel-shaped runner + SPA; global setup runs supabase reset + baseline + demo seed

Login strategy per Q-21: (a) real sign-in through the SPA form with seeded known-password users for login specs; (b) admin-minted sessions via local service-role key injected into browser storage for bulk session setup
Job-trigger hooks: helpers invoking cron:run <job> and draining the queue (queue:worker one-shot or drain call) so alert/expiry specs can force job effects deterministically
Attachment specs adapted to the signed-URL flow; intake specs to the API-key header
Run the complete suite; fix test-infrastructure issues; product-behavior failures are findings against the owning task, not silently patched tests (spec 6.2 discrepancy rule)
Decide + wire e2e-in-CI (full or smoke subset) per runtime budget; document the decision
out_of_scope: New product features or UI changes
Rewriting spec intent (adaptation only — A-17 allows test-infrastructure changes only)
implementation_details: e2e_tests package: update playwright config (baseURL, webServer commands starting local stack + functions + SPA), auth helpers (replace Keycloak login page objects with the SPA /sign-in page object + storageState minting via @supabase/supabase-js admin), seed hooks calling npm scripts.

Admin-minted sessions: create session via Admin API/signInWithPassword server-side, write the supabase-js storage key into localStorage-based storageState; one dedicated spec keeps exercising the real login surface.
Account-enumeration and reset-confirmation semantics verified during adaptation (P-01/spec 16) — record any GoTrue-semantics differences as documented findings.
Deterministic job effects: specs never wait for pg_cron timing; they call the trigger hooks.
Visual shell + a11y specs: expected to pass unchanged (no visual redesign); differences are regressions to fix in owning tasks.
Local login creds for visual checks per project memory remain sourced from the demo seed docs.

unit: None (this task IS the e2e deliverable)
integration: Helper-level checks: admin-minted storageState yields an authenticated page; job hooks produce observable state changes
e2e: Full adapted Playwright suite green against the migrated stack: login, tenant manager, user manager, settings, parties, lead intake/workflow, quotes + attachments, dashboards x5, alerts (incl. clearing via job hooks), reports, exports, tenant isolation, RBAC visibility, role-403 sweep, cross-tenant internal mode, demo journey, a11y, visual shell

findings.summary: SPA api/client.ts parses problem+json errors as Record<string,string[]>, but the migrated backend's spec-mandated contract is errors:[{field,code,message}] - the array makes toNormalizedError throw a TypeError instead of returning a NormalizedError (transferred from T-009 F-009-1).
findings.detail: src/ui/src/api/client.ts:30 declares errors?: Record<string, string[]> and client.ts:53-55 does Object.entries(body.errors).flatMap(([field, messages]) => messages.map(...)). Against the array shape, 'messages' is a {field,code,message} object and messages.map throws BEFORE detail is read, so a populated detail cannot keep the error banner rendering - the caller's promise rejects with a TypeError. Currently latent only because no SPA-facing route exists on the new backend (T-009 serves only /health, and the SPA still calls the .NET API). SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT: the client.ts fix must land before ANY validated endpoint is exposed to the SPA - i.e. no later than T-018's dev-proxy wiring against ported endpoints (T-019+), even though this finding is owned here. Fix: update toNormalizedError to read errors:[{field,code,message}] (optionally tolerating the legacy dictionary during cutover) and add a test asserting a 422 with errors[] yields a NormalizedError with populated fieldErrors.
findings.resolution: Verified already fixed in the current tree (landed in a prior iteration alongside the SPA migration): src/ui/src/api/client.ts now defines `errors?: unknown` and a `toFieldErrors` narrower that reads the array-of-{field,code,message} shape and returns [] for any non-array rather than throwing (the header comment names F-043-1 explicitly). Test coverage exists in src/ui/src/api/client.test.ts: `apiPost_WhenProblemJsonErrorsArrayPresent_ShouldRejectWithNormalizedErrorNotATypeError` and the 422-errors[]→populated-fieldErrors case. No further change required.

Fixed by T-041 (F-041-4): scripts/db/demo-data/catalog.ts now defines the 'admin' role as permissions:'tenant_all' with INTERNAL_ONLY_PERMISSION_PREFIXES (['tenants.','global.']) excluded, and INTERNAL_ROLE (global) carries tenants.*/global.* separately. Re-verified against the demo-seeded DB: pilot.admin (tenant admin) no longer renders the Tenant Manager nav and role-403-sweep produces zero >=400s; tenant-manager.spec.ts:81 (RM sees no Tenant Manager nav + Forbidden deep link) and internal-cross-tenant.spec.ts (only the Internal persona reaches Tenant Manager) both pass. Nav visibility and backend authorization now agree (AC-083).
findings.summary: Demo 'admin' role over-grants: it holds the ENTIRE permission catalog including the Internal/global-only codes (tenants.view, global.*), so a non-Internal tenant admin (pilot.admin@quoteiq.local) renders the Internal-only Tenant Manager nav item, whose GET /api/v1/tenants the backend correctly 403s. Nav visibility (tenant-scoped tenants.view) and backend authorization (global/Internal grant) disagree - exactly the class AC-083/V-083 forbids.
findings.detail: scripts/db/demo-data/catalog.ts TENANT_ROLES gives the 'admin' role permissions:'all', which resolves to every catalog code, including tenants.view / global.view_any_tenant that belong to INTERNAL_ROLE. The SPA nav gates nav-tenant-manager on PermissionCodes.TenantsView and selectHasAnyPermission accepts a TENANT-scoped grant (src/ui/src/app/slices/sessionSlice.ts), so Tenant Manager renders for pilot.admin; the backend GET /tenants is a cross-tenant Internal endpoint and returns 403 to the non-Internal caller (tenant-safe, correct). Observed while adapting role-403-sweep.spec.ts: crawling as Tenant Admin produced repeated `403 GET /api/v1/tenants`. Fix should live in the demo seed (do not grant Internal/global-only codes to a tenant role) and/or the permission catalog scoping (mark tenants.*/global.* as non-tenant-assignable). Not fixed here (product/seed change is out of scope for the e2e adaptation task); pilot.admin was removed from the pure tenant-member sweep and the internal persona covers Tenant Manager via internal.admin's global grant.

findings.resolution: MISDIAGNOSIS confirmed (see F-043-5): the fractional alpha was a CSS-transition timing race, not a translucent design token. The nav pill IS the solid accent at rest. Fixed in visual-shell.spec.ts by polling the computed background-color until the 140ms `transition: background` settles (expect.poll to rgb(21,154,166)) instead of a single mid-flight getComputedStyle read. visual-shell.spec.ts:33 now passes deterministically; the earlier 'owner T-013' attribution was a stale cross-reference to a pre-migration UI-remediation numbering (the current T-013 is an unrelated backend task). No product/CSS change required.
findings.summary: Visual-shell (A-17/V-082): the active sidebar nav pill renders its background at ~62% alpha (rgba(21,154,166,0.62)) instead of the solid accent (#159aa6 = rgb(21,154,166)) the design-system spec asserts. The accent TOKEN is solid in tokens.css and .qiq-nav-item--active sets `background: var(--qiq-accent)`, so the translucency comes from an override/opacity higher in the cascade.
findings.detail: visual-shell.spec.ts:38 reads the computed background-color of `.qiq-nav-item--active` and expects rgb(21,154,166); the running SPA returns rgba(21,154,166,0.62). tokens.css defines --qiq-accent:#159aa6 (light) with no alpha and components.css:327 sets the active background to var(--qiq-accent) solid, so the alpha is applied by another rule/opacity not audited here. Per A-17 the visual shell is expected to pass unchanged, so a difference is a regression to fix in the owning shell/design-system task, not something to loosen in the spec. Left as-is (product/CSS change out of scope for the e2e task).

findings.resolution: Fixed by T-052 (shell pointer-interception): the sidebar nav now scrolls within a bounded region so overflowing nav content no longer paints over / intercepts pointer events for the TenantSwitcher. Re-verified against the demo-seeded DB at 1280x720: shell-nav-overflow.spec.ts (the dedicated F-043-4 regression guard: elementFromPoint at each nav link's centre IS the link, plus real clicks navigate) passes, and tenant-manager.spec.ts:15 / internal-cross-tenant.spec.ts nav clicks to Tenant Manager and User Manager land for the full-nav Internal persona.
findings.summary: GENUINE PRODUCT REGRESSION found among the 16 reds, not adaptation debt: the AppShell/Sidebar/TenantSwitcher CSS layout lets the sidebar nav's overflowing content visually collide with the TenantSwitcher, which paints on top and INTERCEPTS POINTER EVENTS - blocking clicks on the Tenant Manager (and likely User Manager) nav link for admin personas with the full admin nav, in Playwright's default 1280x720 viewport (a very common real laptop resolution).
findings.detail: Reproduced first-hand re-running tenant-manager.spec.ts:15 (V-006): `Error: locator.click: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded ... <select aria-label="Switch tenant">...</select> from <div data-testid="tenant-switcher"> subtree intercepts pointer events` when clicking getByTestId('nav-tenant-manager'). Root cause traced in src/ui/src/components/shell/AppShell.tsx + Sidebar.tsx + theme/components.css: `.qiq-sidebar` (the outer flex column) has `overflow-y:auto; height:100vh`, but its child `<nav>` (rendered by Sidebar.tsx) is given inline `flex:1; minHeight:0` with NO overflow property of its own. When the full admin nav (9 standard items + separator + up to 3 admin items) plus the brand header don't fit the shrunk flex-basis, the nav's list content overflows past its own (shrunk) box with default `overflow:visible` - that overflow is NOT counted by the parent `.qiq-sidebar`'s scroll calculation (only the item's flex-computed box height is), so the overflowing tail of the nav list paints in the same physical region as TenantSwitcher/UserCard, which are later in DOM/paint order and therefore receive the pointer events instead of the nav links underneath them. This is a real, reproducible functional/accessibility defect (admins cannot reach Tenant Manager or User Manager by clicking the nav in a standard-height browser window), not a stale-label or seed-data issue - it does not belong in the 'adaptation debt' bucket the implementor filed the other 15 reds under. Searched every current-numbering task file (T-001..T-051) for ownership of src/ui/src/components/shell/* or theme/components.css: none claims it. F-043-3's 'owner: T-013' is a stale cross-reference to an OLD pre-migration UI-remediation task numbering (per project memory, that plan's T-0xx IDs collide with this migration's task list); the CURRENT T-013 is 'Tenant-context middleware', an unrelated backend task with no UI files in scope. This shell code appears to be pre-existing/inherited SPA code with no owner in the current task list.
findings.suggested_fix: Give `<nav data-testid="sidebar-nav">` its own `overflow-y: auto; min-height: 0` (or similar) so it scrolls internally instead of bleeding into TenantSwitcher/UserCard, OR restructure AppShell so TenantSwitcher/UserCard are pinned via a mechanism that cannot be overpainted by overflowing nav content (e.g. their own stacking context / the nav wrapped in a dedicated scroll region). Needs a dedicated fix task (or T-044 pre-cutover hardening) since no current task owns this file; do not let T-043 or T-044 close with this masquerading as 'documented adaptation debt'.
findings.evidence: Live re-run of the full Playwright suite (npm run test:e2e, chromium project) against the demo-seeded DB produced 52 passed / 15 failed / 54 skipped / 7 did not run; tenant-manager.spec.ts:15 error-context.md captured the exact pointer-event-intercept call log quoted above.

findings.resolution: Fixed: visual-shell.spec.ts's active-nav-pill assertion now polls the computed background-color until the 140ms background transition settles (expect.poll to the solid rgb(21,154,166)) rather than sampling getComputedStyle mid-flight. Re-ran the spec repeatedly — the alpha is consistently 1.0 (solid) at rest, confirming the transition-timing diagnosis and closing F-043-3 as a test-timing issue rather than a CSS override. No animation-disabling hack or weakened assertion; a genuinely translucent pill would still fail.
findings.summary: F-043-3 is likely MISDIAGNOSED: re-running the identical, unmodified visual-shell.spec.ts assertion produced a DIFFERENT alpha value (rgba(21,154,166,0.882)) than the one originally recorded (rgba(21,154,166,0.62)). A real, stable CSS override/opacity rule would reproduce the same alpha every run; two different alpha readings against unchanged code strongly indicates the assertion is reading `getComputedStyle` mid-CSS-transition rather than hitting a genuinely translucent design-token override.
findings.detail: `.qiq-nav-item { transition: background 0.14s, color 0.14s; }` (theme/components.css) animates background-color changes. visual-shell.spec.ts's `beforeEach` only waits for `app-shell` to be visible after `loginAs` (a real SPA sign-in + client-side route to /overview), then the very next test immediately reads `getComputedStyle(...).background-color` with no wait for the transition to settle and no animation-disabling. No `--qiq-*` token or CSS rule anywhere in tokens.css/components.css assigns a literal alpha < 1 or an rgba()/color-mix() to `--qiq-accent` or `.qiq-nav-item--active`'s background (grepped both files) - the only plausible source of a fractional alpha is an in-flight transition interpolating from a transparent/absent background to the solid accent, caught at an arbitrary point in its 140ms window (possibly worsened by React 18 StrictMode's dev-only mount/unmount/remount double-invoke, since e2e runs against `npm run dev`, not a production build, and StrictMode's double-invoke is stripped in production).
findings.suggested_fix: Do not chase a CSS override that may not exist. Make the assertion deterministic: either wait for the `transitionend` event on the element, add a short fixed settle delay before reading computed style, or set `transition: none` for automated test runs (e.g. via a test-only stylesheet or `prefers-reduced-motion` honored in CSS). Re-run after the fix; if the alpha is then consistently 1.0 (solid), close F-043-3 as a test-timing issue rather than a product CSS defect, and remove the incorrect 'owner: T-013' attribution.
findings.evidence: Re-ran visual-shell.spec.ts's active-nav-pill assertion against the unmodified codebase: observed 'Received: rgba(21, 154, 166, 0.882)' vs the implementor's originally recorded 0.62 - same code, same assertion, two different fractional alphas.

findings.resolution: Resolved on two fronts. (1) T-041's tenant_all fix removed the Internal-only over-grant. (2) The evaluator's expectation that settings.spec.ts:23 would then pass unchanged was itself incorrect: a tenant admin (pilot.admin) legitimately holds reference_data.manage, so it is NOT a valid negative case for hiding the Reference data tab. Adapted the spec to the migrated seed's actual minimal-Settings persona — sales.manager, which holds only brokers.view among Settings subsection permissions (SettingsLayout gates Reference data on reference_data.manage, which sales_manager lacks). settings.spec.ts:23 now passes (sees only the Brokers tab; Forbidden on the business-rules deep link), and unblocking it let the rest of the serial Settings suite run green (business rules, business assignments, brokers, reference data).
findings.summary: F-043-2's blast radius is larger than documented: the same demo 'admin' role over-grant (permissions:'all', including Internal-only codes) also breaks settings.spec.ts:23's subsection-gating test, not only the Tenant Manager nav. Confirms F-043-2 is a genuine T-041 seed defect, not a nav-gating logic bug, and that T-041 (currently PASS) has a real open consequence.
findings.detail: settings.spec.ts:23 logs in as pilot.admin@quoteiq.local and asserts `getByTestId('settings-tab-reference-data')).toHaveCount(0)` (a tenant admin with only brokers.manage should not see the Reference Data subsection tab); the live run failed with 'Expected: 0, Received: 1' - the tab IS rendered because pilot.admin's 'admin' role resolves to permissions:'all' per scripts/db/demo-data/catalog.ts:132 (`{ key: 'admin', name: 'Tenant Administrator', permissions: 'all' }`), which includes reference_data.manage and every Internal-only code. Verified the nav/tab-gating LOGIC itself is correct (Sidebar.tsx's NavItemLink hides entirely on `!selectHasAnyPermission`, matching AC-016's 'never rendered disabled' rule) - the defect is purely that the seed hands a tenant-scoped role every permission in the catalog, not that gating fails to check permissions.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix scripts/db/demo-data/catalog.ts's TENANT_ROLES 'admin' definition to exclude Internal/global-only codes (tenants.*, global.*) from a tenant-scoped role's 'all' resolution, or scope 'all' to only tenant-assignable codes. Once fixed, tenant-manager nav visibility AND settings.spec.ts's subsection-gating assertion should both pass unchanged.
findings.evidence: settings-settings-subsecti-ad11f error-context.md: 'Locator: getByTestId("settings-tab-reference-data") Expected: 0 Received: 1'; scripts/db/demo-data/catalog.ts:132 read directly.

findings.summary: Demo-seed fixture extensions needed to un-fixme five e2e scenarios that are seed-data-blocked (not product defects). The migrated UI is correct in every case; the seed simply lacks the data shape the assertion needs. Accepted as MVP debt by the evaluator, tracked here so it is not silently dropped.
findings.detail: Each is marked test.fixme with an inline SEED GAP reason in the spec. (a) NON-BWP TENANT: both demo tenants are BWP, so shell.spec.ts:58 (AC-074 display-currency for a non-admin, non-BWP member) stays skipped; add a third tenant with a non-BWP currency and a member lacking business_rules.view. (b) FALLING-TREND DELTAS: the demo set has no favourable falling metric, so dashboard-overview.spec.ts's 'turnaround green delta' (the live run renders a RISING '↑ +0.2') and dashboard-loss.spec.ts's 'falling lost-premium delta' (no prior-period comparison, so KpiCard renders no kpi-delta at all) can't assert the green LowerIsBetter delta; seed a prior-period-comparable falling metric. (c) COMPETITOR ROWS: the demo Closed-Lost set records no competitor premium/name, so dashboard-loss.spec.ts's competitor table renders zero competitor-row; seed lost leads with competitor data. (d) PRE/POST-QUOTE LOSSES: dashboard-loss.spec.ts's reason-drill 'before/after-quote column' needs lost leads spanning both sides of the quote boundary; seed pre- and post-quote losses. (e) ZERO-MEMBERSHIP INTERNAL PERSONA + 3RD TENANT: internal-cross-tenant.spec.ts (V-084) was adapted to internal.admin (a member of both tenants), so the original memberless-Internal-switches-into-a-NON-member-tenant leg cannot be reproduced; add a zero-membership Internal persona and a tenant it is not a member of to restore that exact leg. Fix lives entirely in scripts/db/demo-data (no product change).

findings.summary: Alerts-center e2e fixtures: two Alerts scenarios are seed-condition-blocked (not product defects). The Alerts UI, action labels, and badge slice are correct; the seed lacks the specific alert/visit conditions the assertions need. Accepted as MVP debt by the evaluator.
findings.detail: Both marked test.fixme with inline SEED GAP reasons. (a) ASSIGN & ACKNOWLEDGE FLOW (alerts-center.spec.ts:41, V-061): the assign->clear->highlighted-quote leg times out waiting for an unassigned-lead alert row carrying the 'Assign & acknowledge' action within reach of the default 'All' queue for the Sales Manager. Verified the label IS correct (actionForAlertType('unassigned_lead')='assign', ALERT_ACTION_LABELS.assign='Assign & acknowledge' in src/ui/src/features/alerts/alertsApi.ts) and the seed DOES fire unassigned_lead alerts (405 in tenant 1) — the gap is that no actionable unassigned-lead alert is deterministically present/reachable in the persona's default queue view. Seed one guaranteed-actionable unassigned-lead alert for this persona at the top of the queue. (b) NEW-SINCE-LAST-VISIT BADGE (alerts-center.spec.ts:82, V-062): the per-user badge needs a seeded last-alerts-visit baseline older than a batch of alerts so a non-zero count renders; the seed sets no per-user alert-visit timestamp. Seed a new-since-last-visit condition per badge persona. Both are seed/fixture concerns owned by the alerts feature/seed; the badge slice, polling, and reset thunks are already unit/component-covered.

findings.summary: internal-cross-tenant.spec.ts's docstring overstates existing coverage: it claims 'a tenant admin (pilot.admin...) sees no Tenant Manager nav and is Forbidden on the deep link (tenant-manager.spec.ts)', but tenant-manager.spec.ts's negative-access test signs in as rm.tebogo (a Relationship Manager), never pilot.admin. No committed spec directly exercises the specific persona (pilot.admin, the tenant admin) that was the actual subject of F-041-4/F-043-2/F-043-6.
findings.detail: Grepped every spec file for 'pilot.admin': it appears in api-access.spec.ts (unrelated flow), settings.spec.ts (only in a comment explaining why it's NOT used as the Reference-data negative case), internal-cross-tenant.spec.ts (only in the docstring's claim, not in any executable step), and role-403-sweep.spec.ts (only in a comment explaining why pilot.admin is EXCLUDED from the sweep -- and that comment is itself now stale/misleading, since it cites F-043-2 as if the over-grant it describes were still current: 'The demo admin role (pilot.admin) is deliberately excluded: T-041 grants it the ENTIRE permission catalog, including the Internal/global-only codes' -- that grant no longer exists post-fix (T-041 F-041-4); the comment should be updated to explain the CURRENT reason for exclusion, i.e. the sweep is scoped to PURE tenant-member roles and pilot.admin's tenant_all role, while corrected, is intentionally out of scope for a different reason now (it is the migrated-seed's own scope choice, not a workaround for a bug). I independently wrote and ran an ad hoc Playwright check (not committed) against the live demo-seeded app: logged in as pilot.admin@quoteiq.local, asserted getByTestId('nav-tenant-manager') has count 0, and asserted a deep link to /admin/tenants renders the Forbidden page -- both passed, confirming the underlying product behavior is correct. The gap is purely in the committed suite's own coverage/documentation, not a product defect.
findings.evidence: grep -n "pilot.admin" across e2e_tests/tests/*.ts; direct ad hoc reproduction (test file created, run, and deleted during this evaluation, not committed) confirmed nav-tenant-manager count=0 and Forbidden on /admin/tenants for pilot.admin against the demo-seeded DB.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a direct assertion for pilot.admin (no Tenant Manager nav, Forbidden on /admin/tenants deep link) to tenant-manager.spec.ts's existing negative-access test (or a new one), and correct the docstring/comment cross-references in internal-cross-tenant.spec.ts and role-403-sweep.spec.ts to point at the corrected reality post-F-041-4 rather than the resolved-but-still-quoted F-043-2 over-grant language. Non-blocking: the evaluator independently verified the actual behavior is correct.

results.f_043_7_f_043_8_disposition: Both ruled genuinely acceptable MVP fixme debt, not must-build-now. In each case the rendering/action-label code path was read directly and confirmed already correct (KpiCard only renders kpi-delta when delta!==null; ALERT_ACTION_LABELS.assign is correct) -- the gap is exclusively that the seed lacks a specific data shape (a falling-trend metric, competitor rows, an actionable queued alert, a visit-timestamp baseline), not a missing feature. None of the 6 fixme specs these unblock are required for AC-090/AC-092's nav/RBAC journeys. F-043-7 is scoped to T-041's file surface (scripts/db/demo-data/*) and is better handled as a small dedicated T-041 follow-up task than by reopening T-041 in this round (see T-041's own evaluation entry for this recommendation). F-043-8 stays owned by T-037 as filed.
results.ac_090_ac_092_dod_assessment: AC-092 (Q-21 dual login: real-form spec + admin-minted sessions, no external identity dependency) is honestly satisfied -- login.spec.ts exercises the real SPA form and the bulk of the suite uses admin-minted storageState via the service-role key, both independently confirmed running.
